findings.title: R2 limb (a) metric normalization is unpinned after the control-book amendment: index-point control vs USD net arm can be compared at 0.5x only under a convention nobody has pinned
findings.description: The remediation correctly breaks the v1 tautology by re-specifying the A4-P2 control as a zero-cost VIX index-point book. But evaluate_r2's limb (a) consumes arm_expectancy_net_tier2 (USD, net of execution costs on ETP legs) against index_control_expectancy_net_tier2 (VIX index points, no costs) under the frozen text 'out-earns the arm same-sign at >= 0.5x per round trip'. The comparison is dimensionally meaningful only under an unstated normalization (e.g., both expressed as per-round-trip return fractions on comparable exposure); the addendum's declared_convention pins the BOOK unit ('1 unit = 1.0 point') but NOT the metric normalization, the evaluator takes raw floats, and the test fixtures (PASSING_METRICS arm 0.02 vs control -0.01) silently assume same-scale numbers. A naive E-phase supplier using native units (VIX ~ 20 points vs USD on 10k notional legs) would make the veto fire (almost) never; a different normalization could flip R2 verdicts for the 3 A4-P2 cells. Same defect class as v1 M1 (unpinned convention governing a kill route). REQUIRED before any E-phase R2 verdict on an A4-P2 cell: pin the normalization convention pre-score via the same disclosed addendum mechanism (e.g., 'both expectancies as per-round-trip return fractions: index points divided by entry close; arm net USD divided by entry notional'). Does not invalidate the remediation (the tautology is gone; the comparison is genuine once normalized); zero structural death either way.
